title: Dentogenic infections in spondylodiscitis: The significance of odontogenic foci
summary: Inflammation of the spine, known as spondylodiscitis, is a serious condition that is often associated with severe pain, long hospital stays and sometimes permanent damage. In almost half of all cases, doctors are unable to identify a clear cause for the infection. There is evidence to suggest that inflammation in the mouth or teeth may play a role, but this has rarely been investigated to date. With this study, we want to find out how often such infections occur in the mouth of patients with spondylodiscitis. To this end, an additional examination by a dentist and a special X-ray (OPG) will be carried out during the hospital stay. The results will be compared with data from the general population. The aim is to better understand the causes of this disease and thus enable more targeted treatments in the future.

interventions.name:
Patients with confirmed spondylodiscitis; no intervention
Observation period per patient: total of 3 months 

Time points of assessment:
- Baseline assessment during inpatient stay
- Dental examination (clinical oral health assessment)
- Orthopantomogram (OPG) to identify potential oral infect

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Diagnosed spondylodiscitis (clinical and imaging), able to walk and stand
Exclusion criteria:
Pregnancy, immobility (inability to walk or stand)
